summary: Steel 100-foot Aermotor tower beside the Village Museum in McClellanville, SC; builder and date disputed (1940 vs 1930s); Town-owned, condition assessment funded in 2025.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor tower with a cab about 7 by 7 feet

events.note: Register gives 1940 and says the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service erected it; the Town's 2025 RFQ says it was constructed in the 1930s for the U.S. Biological Survey (see notes_for_editor)
Withstood Hurricane Hugo, which damaged the forests around it
Registered July 1, 1995 as US 121, SC 1; first South Carolina lookout on the register
July 2025 FFLA restoration grant of $500 to the Town for a comprehensive condition assessment; the Town's RFQ seeks bid-ready stabilization plans

notes_for_editor: Builder and date disagree: the Register gives 1940 and the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service; the Town's RFQ gives the 1930s and the U.S. Biological Survey. Both are cited, not resolved. Staffing end date is unknown ('until recent years'). Access is unknown: no source read says whether the public may visit or climb. Record coordinates match the Register's; elevation 7.6 m matches 25 ft. Unfetched search snippets (a Village Museum Facebook post, a Town picture PDF with no text layer) suggest c. 1935 and Forestry Commission use into the early 1980s; not used in the story. Worth a human look: the FFLA report's '$14,000 matching' phrase is broken across lines and was not used.
